summary: Review-required audit trail for the live USB selective suspend card. The app already exposes a command-backed powercfg implementation, and repo docs plus provenance overrides map the tweak id to USB power-management research, but the card still lives only in the first-party provider and has not yet been promoted into the validated research-provider surface.

setting.name: Disable USB Selective Suspend
setting.casual_explanation: This keeps Windows from selectively suspending USB devices through the active power plan, which can help when USB devices disconnect or sleep unexpectedly.
setting.why_people_change_it: People change it when they are troubleshooting flaky USB devices or want to keep attached devices fully awake.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: It can improve USB stability, but it can also increase power use because USB devices stay more active. The live app is already reversible, but the card has not yet been promoted into the research-provider surface.
setting.professional_notes: The current app models this as a powercfg-backed command tweak that reads the active scheme's USB selective suspend values, applies 0 for both AC and DC, and restores the previous snapshot on rollback. Repo power docs and tweak-provenance overrides both map the tweak id to USB power-management research. The record stays review-required until the command-backed power lane is promoted into the validated research-provider surface.
